summary:
This is Part 133 of a series on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Ibn al-Qayyim, led by Sheikh Ali Mashhour. The lecture focuses on the miracles of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) beyond the Quran, explaining their purpose and significance. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that miracles serve two main functions: to prove the validity of the Prophet's claim to prophethood and to strengthen the hearts of believers during critical times. The lecture discusses various miracles including the splitting of the moon, water gushing from the Prophet's fingers, food increasing to feed many, inanimate objects speaking in exaltation, trees moving to provide privacy, and poisoned food that warned the Prophet of its toxicity.

Sh. Ali Mashhour stresses the importance of understanding not just the words of the Quran and Sunnah, but their correct meanings as intended by Allah and the Prophet. He explains that miracles are by nature inexplicable—their value lies in being beyond human comprehension—and that belief in miracles distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever. The lecture also addresses criticism from skeptics and emphasizes that Allah preserves both the words and proper understanding of His message through scholars throughout time who carry forward the knowledge and implementation of the Sunnah correctly.
suggested_title: The Miracles of Prophet Muhammad: Beyond the Quran - Part 133 of Zadul-Ma'ad
